title.en: General of the Right Golden Guard

sourceDate.text: 天祐二年七月十三日夜
天祐二年七月十三日夜

units.zh: 列傳第一百三十一
units.en: Biography 131
units.literal: Biography 131

units.zh: 史憲誠 子孝章 何進滔 子弘敬 韓允忠 子簡 樂彥禎 子從訓 羅弘信 子威
units.en: Shi Xiancheng and his son Xiaozhang; He Jintao and his son Hongjing; Han Yunzhong and his son Jian; Le Yanzhen and his son Congxun; Luo Hongxin and his son Wei
units.literal: Shi Xiancheng; his son Xiaozhang; He Jintao; his son Hongjing; Han Yunzhong; his son Jian; Le Yanzhen; his son Congxun; Luo Hongxin; his son Wei

units.zh: 史憲誠，其先出於奚虜，今為靈武建康人。
units.en: Shi Xiancheng's family originally came from the Xi people; he was registered as a native of Jiankang in Lingwu.
units.literal: Shi Xiancheng—his ancestors came from the Xi barbarians; he is now registered as a native of Jiankang in Lingwu.

units.zh: 祖道德，開府儀同三司、試太常卿、上柱國、懷澤郡王。
units.en: His grandfather Daode had been Grand General with Honorary Staff of Three Offices, Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Supreme Pillar of State, and Duke of Huaize.
units.literal: His grandfather Daode held the titles Grand General with Honorary Staff of Three Offices, Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Supreme Pillar of State, and Duke of Huaize commandery.

units.zh: 父周洛，為魏博軍校，事田季安，至兵馬大使、銀青光祿大夫、檢校太子賓客、兼御史中丞、柱國、北海郡王。
units.en: His father Zhou Luo had served as a Wei-Bo regimental officer under Tian Ji'an, eventually reaching Army-and-Horse Commissioner, Silver-Gleam Glory Grand Master, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of State, and King of Beihai.
units.literal: His father Zhou Luo was a Wei-Bo military officer serving Tian Ji'an, rising to Army-and-Horse Commissioner, Silver-Gleam Glory Grand Master, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of State, and King of Beihai commandery.

units.zh: 憲誠始以材勇，隨父歷軍中右職，兼監察御史。
units.en: Xiancheng first distinguished himself by talent and courage, rising through senior army posts alongside his father, and also held the post of Investigating Censor.
units.literal: Xiancheng at first by talent and valor followed his father through senior military posts, and concurrently served as Investigating Censor.

units.zh: 元和中，田弘正討李師道，令憲誠以先鋒四千人濟河，累下其城柵。
units.en: During the Yuanhe era, when Tian Hongzheng marched against Li Shidao, he sent Xiancheng with four thousand vanguard troops across the river; they took one enemy stockade after another.
units.literal: In the Yuanhe reign, Tian Hongzheng campaigned against Li Shidao and ordered Xiancheng with four thousand vanguard troops to cross the river, repeatedly taking their walled stockades.

units.zh: 復以大軍齊進，乘勢逐北，魏之全師迫於鄆之城下。
units.en: The main army then advanced in force. Riding the momentum of victory, he pursued the enemy until the entire Wei force stood before the walls of Yan.
units.literal: Again with the main army advancing together, seizing the momentum he pursued north; Wei's full army pressed to below the walls of Yan.

units.zh: 師道窮蹙，劉悟斬首投魏軍。
units.en: Shidao was cornered; Liu Wu cut off his head and turned it over to the Wei forces.
units.literal: Shidao was driven to extremity; Liu Wu beheaded him and surrendered the head to the Wei army.

units.zh: 錄功，超授憲誠兼中丞。
units.en: For his merit he was specially promoted to concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: Recording merit, Xiancheng was exceptionally appointed concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 鎮州王承宗死，弘正自魏移領鎮州。
units.en: When Wang Chengzong of Zhenzhou died, Hongzheng left Wei to assume control of Zhenzhou.
units.literal: Wang Chengzong of Zhenzhou died; Hongzheng shifted from Wei to take charge of Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 居數月，為王廷湊所殺，遂以兵叛。
units.en: Within a few months Hongzheng was murdered by Wang Tingcou, who then rose in armed rebellion.
units.literal: After several months he was killed by Wang Tingcou, who then rebelled with troops.

units.zh: 朝廷以弘正子布為魏博節度使，領兵討伐，俾復父冤。
units.en: The court appointed Hongzheng's son Bu military governor of Wei-Bo and sent him to campaign against the rebels so he might avenge his father.
units.literal: The court made Hongzheng's son Bu Wei-Bo military governor and led troops to punish the rebels, enabling him to avenge his father.

units.zh: 時幽州硃克融援助廷湊，布不能制，因自引決，軍情囂然。
units.en: Zhu Kerong of Youzhou was then supporting Tingcou. Bu could not bring the situation under control and took his own life, leaving the army in turmoil.
units.literal: At the time Youzhou's Zhu Kerong aided Tingcou; Bu could not control the situation and therefore took his own life; army sentiment was turbulent.

units.zh: 憲誠為中軍都知兵馬使，乘亂以河朔舊事動其人心，諸軍即擁而歸魏，共立為帥，國家因而命之。
units.en: Xiancheng was commander of the central army. Exploiting the chaos, he appealed to old Hebei loyalties and swayed the troops. The armies acclaimed him, returned to Wei, and made him their commander; the court thereupon confirmed the appointment.
units.literal: Xiancheng was Central Army Commissioner for Military Affairs; seizing the disorder he stirred their hearts with old Hebei stories, and the armies at once acclaimed him and returned to Wei, jointly installing him as commander—the state then appointed him.

units.zh: 時克融、廷湊並據兵為亂，憲誠喜得旄節，雖外順朝旨，而中與硃、王為輔車之勢，長慶二年正月也。
units.en: Kerong and Tingcou were both in rebellion with their armies. Xiancheng was pleased to receive the commissioner's symbols of authority. Though he outwardly obeyed the court, inwardly he and Zhu and Wang were bound together like linked chariots. This was in the first month of Changqing 2 (822).
units.literal: At the time Kerong and Tingcou both held troops in rebellion; Xiancheng rejoiced to receive the ceremonial staff and banner, and though outwardly compliant with court intent, inwardly he and Zhu and Wang were mutual support like linked chariots—it was the first month of Changqing year two.

units.zh: 尋遣司門郎中韋文恪宣慰。
units.en: Before long the court sent Director of the Bureau of Gates Wei Wenke as imperial envoy to offer reassurance.
units.literal: Soon the court dispatched Director of the Bureau of Gates Wei Wenke to proclaim consolation.

units.zh: 時李㝏為亂，與憲誠書問交通。
units.en: Li Zong was then in rebellion and was exchanging messages with Xiancheng.
units.literal: At the time Li Zong was in rebellion and exchanged letters with Xiancheng.

units.zh: 憲誠表請與㝏節鉞，仍於黎陽艤舟，示欲渡河。
units.en: Xiancheng petitioned the throne to share military authority with Li Zong and moored boats at Liyang as though preparing to cross the river.
units.literal: Xiancheng memorialized asking to share ceremonial authority with Zong, and moreover moored boats at Liyang, showing intent to cross the river.

units.zh: 及見文恪，舉止驕倨，其言甚悖。
units.en: When he received Wenke, his manner was arrogant and his words openly defiant.
units.literal: When he met Wenke his bearing was arrogant and insolent; his words were very rebellious.

units.zh: 旋聞絺為帳下所殺，乃從改過，謂文恪曰：「憲誠蕃人，猶狗也，唯能識主。
units.en: When he soon learned that Li Zong had been killed by his own men, he changed his tune and told Wenke, "Xiancheng is a barbarian—no better than a dog, and a dog knows only its master.
units.literal: Soon hearing that Zong was killed by his own subordinates, he then followed and changed course, saying to Wenke: "Xiancheng is a barbarian, still like a dog—only able to recognize its master.

units.zh: 雖被棒打，終不忍離。」
units.en: Even when beaten with a stick, it will not willingly leave its master's side."
units.literal: Even though beaten with a stick, in the end he cannot bear to leave."

units.zh: 其狡譎如此。
units.en: Such was the extent of his cunning and duplicity.
units.literal: His crafty deceit was like this.

units.zh: 朝廷每為優容，尋加左僕射。
units.en: The court repeatedly indulged him, and soon promoted him to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: The court repeatedly showed him forbearance; soon he was additionally made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 敬宗即位，進秩司空。
units.en: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, Xiancheng was promoted to Minister of Works.
units.literal: When Emperor Jingzong acceded, his rank advanced to Minister of Works.

units.zh: 太和二年，滄景節度使李全略卒，其子同捷竊據軍城，表邀符節，舉兵伐之。
units.en: In Taihe 2 (828) the Cangjing military governor Li Quanlue died. His son Tongjie seized the garrison city, petitioned for the commissioner's credentials, and an army was raised to campaign against him.
units.literal: In Taihe year two the Cangjing military governor Li Quanlue died; his son Tongjie seized the army city by stealth, memorialized requesting the tally and staff, and raised troops to campaign against him.

units.zh: 先是，憲誠與全略婚媾，及同捷叛，復潛以糧餉為助。
units.en: Xiancheng had earlier been connected to Quanlue by marriage. When Tongjie rebelled, he secretly sent him grain and supplies.
units.literal: Earlier Xiancheng had been allied by marriage with Quanlue; when Tongjie rebelled, he again secretly supplied grain and provisions as aid.

units.zh: 上屢發使申諭，尋又就加平章事。
units.en: The emperor repeatedly sent envoys to warn him, yet soon promoted him to Grand Councilor as well.
units.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent envoys to admonish and instruct; soon he was additionally made Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 憲誠嘗遣驍將至闕下，恣為張大，宰相韋處厚以語折剉之，憲誠不敢復與同捷為應。
units.en: Xiancheng once sent bold generals to the capital to boast of his power. Grand Councilor Wei Chuhou rebuked them sharply, and Xiancheng dared not coordinate with Tongjie again.
units.literal: Xiancheng once sent fierce generals to the capital gates, wantonly making grand claims; Grand Councilor Wei Chuhou rebuffed him with words, and Xiancheng dared not again respond in concert with Tongjie.

units.zh: 時憲誠示出師共討同捷。
units.en: Xiancheng then made a show of taking the field against Tongjie.
units.literal: At the time Xiancheng made a show of marching out to join in punishing Tongjie.

units.zh: 及滄景平，加司徒。
units.en: When Cangjing was pacified, he was promoted to Minister of Education.
units.literal: When Cangjing was pacified, he was additionally made Minister of Education.

units.zh: 憲誠心不自安，乃遣子孝章入覲，又飛章願以所管奉命。
units.en: Uneasy in his own mind, Xiancheng sent his son Xiaozhang to the capital and urgently petitioned to surrender his command to the throne.
units.literal: Xiancheng's heart was not at ease; he then sent his son Xiaozhang to court audience, and also sent urgent memorials wishing to place what he governed at the court's command.

units.zh: 上嘉之。
units.en: The emperor praised his loyalty.
units.literal: The emperor commended this.

units.zh: 乃加侍中，移鎮河中。
units.en: Xiancheng was made Palace Attendant and transferred to the Hezhong command.
units.literal: He was then additionally made Palace Attendant and transferred to garrison at Hezhong.

units.zh: 憲誠素懷向背，不能以忠誠感激其眾。
units.en: Xiancheng had long been of two minds, and he could not win his troops over with genuine loyalty.
units.literal: Xiancheng had long harbored divided loyalties and could not move his followers with sincere loyalty.

units.zh: 未及出城，太和三年六月二十六日夜，為軍眾所害，冊贈太尉。
units.en: Before he could even leave the city, on the night of the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month of Taihe 3 (829) his own troops killed him. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: Before he could leave the city, on the night of the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month of Taihe year three he was killed by the army masses; posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 孝章，幼聰悟好學。
units.en: Xiaozhang was clever and studious from childhood.
units.literal: Xiaozhang from youth was clever and perceptive and fond of learning.

units.zh: 元和中，李醞為魏帥，取大將子弟列於軍籍。
units.en: During the Yuanhe era, when Li Yun commanded Wei, he enrolled the sons of senior officers on the army rolls.
units.literal: In the Yuanhe reign Li Yun was Wei commander; he took great generals' sons and younger brothers and enrolled them on the army register.

units.zh: 孝章倡言願效文職，醞奇之，令攝府參軍。
units.en: Xiaozhang spoke up saying he wished to serve in a civil post. Yun was impressed and appointed him acting staff adjutant.
units.literal: Xiaozhang took the lead in declaring he wished to serve in civil office; Yun marveled at this and ordered him to act as staff adjutant.

units.zh: 及憲誠領節鉞，改士曹參軍、兼監察御史，賜緋。
units.en: When Xiancheng received his commission, Xiaozhang was made staff officer in the Bureau of Personnel and concurrent Investigating Censor, with scarlet robes bestowed on him.
units.literal: When Xiancheng received the ceremonial staff and banner, he was changed to Staff Officer in the Bureau of Personnel, concurrent Investigating Censor, and granted scarlet robes.

units.zh: 孝章以父在鎮多違朝旨，嘗雪涕極諫，備陳逆順之理。
units.en: Because his father at his post often defied the court, Xiaozhang once wept as he remonstrated with him at length on the difference between loyalty and rebellion.
units.literal: Xiaozhang because his father at the garrison often violated court intent, once wept tears of remonstrance in extreme admonition, fully setting forth the principle of rebellion and obedience.

units.zh: 朝廷聞而嘉之，乃授檢校太子左諭德、兼侍御史，充節度副使。
units.en: When the court learned of this it praised him, appointing him Acting Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, concurrent Attending Censor, and deputy military governor.
units.literal: The court heard and commended this; he was then appointed Acting Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent, concurrent Attending Censor, and serving as military governor's deputy.

units.zh: 累遷至散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，賜紫。
units.en: He rose in due course to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, with purple robes bestowed on him.
units.literal: By successive promotion he reached Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and was granted purple robes.

units.zh: 領本道兵同平滄景，加工部尚書。
units.en: Leading troops from his circuit, he helped pacify Cangjing and was made Minister of Works.
units.literal: Leading this circuit's troops he jointly pacified Cangjing, and was additionally made Minister of Works.

units.zh: 尋請赴闕，文宗慰勞甚厚，憲誠亦因懇乞朝覲。
units.en: He soon asked to go to the capital, where Emperor Wenzong received him with generous praise. Xiancheng also earnestly petitioned for permission to come to court.
units.literal: Soon he requested to go to court; Emperor Wenzong consoled and rewarded him very generously, and Xiancheng also by earnest plea begged court audience.

units.zh: 上知憲誠之入覲，自孝章之謀，遂加禮部尚書，分相、衛、澶三州別為一鎮，俾孝章領之。
units.en: The emperor knew that Xiancheng's visit was Xiaozhang's doing. He promoted Xiaozhang to Minister of Rites, carved out Xiang, Wei, and Chan prefectures as a separate command, and put Xiaozhang in charge of it.
units.literal: The emperor knew Xiancheng's coming to audience stemmed from Xiaozhang's plan; he then additionally made him Minister of Rites, separated Xiang, Wei, and Chan prefectures into a separate command, and had Xiaozhang lead it.

units.zh: 孝章未到鎮，憲誠遇害。
units.en: Before Xiaozhang could take up his new post, Xiancheng was killed.
units.literal: Xiaozhang had not yet reached his command when Xiancheng met violent death.

units.zh: 上以孝章有忠節，起復為右金吾衛將軍。
units.en: Honoring Xiaozhang's loyalty, the emperor recalled him from mourning to serve as General of the Right Golden Guard.
units.literal: The emperor because Xiaozhang had loyal integrity recalled him from mourning to be General of the Right Golden Guard.

units.zh: 間歲，授鄜坊節度使。
units.en: A year later he was appointed military governor of Fufang.
units.literal: Within a year he was appointed military governor of Fufang.

units.zh: 居四年，遷於滑。
units.en: After four years he was transferred to the Hua command.
units.literal: After four years he was transferred to Hua.

units.zh: 一歲，入為右領軍大將軍，改右金吾大將軍，俄授邠寧節度。
units.en: After one year he was recalled to the capital as Grand General of the Right Leading Army, then transferred to Grand General of the Right Golden Guard, and soon after was appointed military governor of Binning.
units.literal: After one year he entered court as Grand General of the Right Leading Army, was changed to Grand General of the Right Golden Guard, and soon was appointed military governor of Binning.

units.zh: 孝章歷三鎮，雖無異績，而謹身畏法，以保初終。
units.en: Xiaozhang held three commands. He won no great distinction, but by living carefully within the law he preserved himself from first to last.
units.literal: Xiaozhang served three commands; though without extraordinary achievement, he was cautious in person and feared the law, thereby preserving his beginning and end.

units.zh: 開成三年十月卒，贈右僕射。
units.en: He died in the tenth month of Kaicheng 3 (838) and was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: In the tenth month of Kaicheng year three he died; posthumously given Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 何進滔，靈武人也。
units.en: He Jintao was a native of Lingwu.
units.literal: He Jintao was a native of Lingwu.

units.zh: 曾祖孝物，祖俊，並本州軍校。
units.en: His great-grandfather Xiaowu and grandfather Jun had both been military officers in their home prefecture.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Xiaowu and grandfather Jun were both military officers of the native prefecture.

units.zh: 父默，夏州衙前兵馬使，檢校太子賓客，試太常卿。
units.en: His father Mo had been Army-and-Horse Commissioner at the Xiazhou yamen, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, and Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
units.literal: His father Mo was Xiazhou Yamen Front Army-and-Horse Commissioner, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, and Acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

units.zh: 以進滔之貴，贈左散騎常侍。
units.en: When Jintao rose to prominence, Mo was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
units.literal: Because of Jintao's eminence, Mo was posthumously given Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 進滔客寄於魏，委質軍門，事節度使田弘正。
units.en: Jintao had come to Wei as a guest and entered military service under the military governor Tian Hongzheng.
units.literal: Jintao sojourned as a guest in Wei, pledged himself at the army gates, and served military governor Tian Hongzheng.

units.zh: 弘正奉詔討鄆州，破李師道，時進滔為衙內都知兵馬使，以功授兼侍御史。
units.en: When Hongzheng campaigned against Yan at the court's order and defeated Li Shidao, Jintao was commissioner of military affairs within the yamen and was made concurrent Attending Censor for his service.
units.literal: Hongzheng received the edict to campaign against Yanzhou and defeated Li Shidao; at the time Jintao was Yamen Inner Commissioner for Military Affairs, and for merit was appointed concurrent Attending Censor.

units.zh: 太和三年，軍眾害史憲誠，連聲而呼曰：「得衙內都知兵馬使何端公知留後，即三軍安矣。」
units.en: In Taihe 3 (829) the troops killed Shi Xiancheng and shouted as one, "If Lord He Duangong, commissioner of military affairs within the yamen, becomes acting regent, the whole army will be secure."
units.literal: In Taihe year three the army masses killed Shi Xiancheng, calling out in unison: "If we get Yamen Inner Commissioner for Military Affairs Lord He Duangong as acting regent, then the three armies will be at peace."

units.zh: 推而立之。
units.en: They acclaimed him and installed him in command.
units.literal: They pushed and installed him.

units.zh: 朝廷因授進滔左散騎常侍、魏博等州節度觀察處置等使。
units.en: The court thereupon appointed Jintao Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and military governor of Wei-Bo and associated prefectures.
units.literal: The court thereupon appointed Jintao Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and military governor, observation commissioner, and disposition commissioner of Wei-Bo and other prefectures.

units.zh: 為魏帥十餘年，大得民情，累官至司徒、平章事卒。
units.en: He commanded Wei for more than ten years and won the people's affection. He rose in due course to Minister of Education and Grand Councilor, and died in office.
units.literal: As Wei commander for more than ten years he greatly won popular sentiment; by successive offices he reached Minister of Education and Grand Councilor and died.

units.zh: 子弘敬襲其位。
units.en: His son Hongjing succeeded him.
units.literal: His son Hongjing succeeded to his position.

units.zh: 朝廷時遣河中帥李執方、滄州帥劉約各遣使勸令歸闕，別俟朝旨。
units.en: The court repeatedly sent envoys through Li Zhifang of Hezhong and Liu Yue of Cangzhou urging him to come to the capital and await further orders.
units.literal: The court at times sent Hezhong commander Li Zhifang and Cangzhou commander Liu Yue each to dispatch envoys urging him to return to court and await separate court instructions.

units.zh: 弘敬不從，竟就加節制。
units.en: Hongjing refused, and in the end received the full commission.
units.literal: Hongjing did not comply, and in the end was given the commissioner's control.

units.zh: 及劉稹反，不時起兵。
units.en: When Liu Zhen rebelled, he failed to mobilize his troops promptly.
units.literal: When Liu Zhen rebelled, he did not raise troops at the proper time.

units.zh: 鎮州王元逵下邢、洺二州，兵次上黨，弘敬方出師壓境。
units.en: Wang Yuankui of Zhenzhou had already taken Xing and Ming, and his army had reached Shangdang, before Hongjing finally marched out to threaten the border.
units.literal: Zhenzhou's Wang Yuankui took Xing and Ming prefectures; troops reached Shangdang; only then did Hongjing march out to press the border.

units.zh: 大中後，宣宗務其姑息，繼加官爵，亦至使相。
units.en: After the Dazhong era Emperor Xuanzong indulged him with successive promotions until he too reached the rank of commissioner-councilor.
units.literal: After the Dazhong reign, Emperor Xuanzong pursued indulgent treatment of him, successively adding offices and ranks until he too reached commissioner and councilor.

units.zh: 咸通初，卒。
units.en: He died early in the Xiantong era (860).
units.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he died.

units.zh: 子全皞嗣之。
units.en: His son Quanhao succeeded him.
units.literal: His son Quanhao succeeded him.

units.zh: 朝廷尋降符節，累官亦至同平章事。
units.en: The court soon issued him the commissioner's credentials, and he too rose in due course to concurrent Grand Councilor.
units.literal: The court soon bestowed tally and staff; by successive offices he too reached concurrent Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 十一年，為軍人所害。
units.en: In year eleven he was killed by his own troops.
units.literal: In year eleven he was killed by the military men.

units.zh: 子孫相繼，四十餘年。
units.en: Father and son had held the post in succession for more than forty years.
units.literal: Sons and grandsons succeeded one another for more than forty years.

units.zh: 韓允忠，魏州人也。
units.en: Han Yunzhong was a native of Weizhou.
units.literal: Han Yunzhong was a native of Weizhou.

units.zh: 舊名君雄，懿宗改賜今名。
units.en: His original name was Junxiong; Emperor Yizong gave him his present name.
units.literal: His former name was Junxiong; Emperor Yizong changed and bestowed the present name.

units.zh: 父國昌，歷本州右職。
units.en: His father Guochang had held senior posts in the local army.
units.literal: His father Guochang passed through senior posts of the native prefecture.

units.zh: 會昌中，從何弘敬破劉稹，以功為貝州刺史、兼御史中丞。
units.en: During the Huichang era he followed He Hongjing in defeating Liu Zhen and was made prefect of Bei and concurrent Censor-in-Chief for his service.
units.literal: In the Huichang reign he followed He Hongjing in defeating Liu Zhen; for merit he became prefect of Bei prefecture and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 以允忠故，累贈兵部尚書。
units.en: Because of Yunzhong's eminence, Guochang was posthumously promoted in stages to Minister of War.
units.literal: Because of Yunzhong, he was by successive gifts made Minister of War.

units.zh: 允忠少仕軍門，繼升裨校。
units.en: Yunzhong entered military service young and rose through the ranks to deputy commander.
units.literal: Yunzhong from youth served at the army gates and successively rose to deputy commander.

units.zh: 潞州之役，亦與其行。
units.en: He also took part in the Luzhou campaign.
units.literal: In the Luzhou campaign he also went with them.

units.zh: 咸通十一年，何全皞為軍眾所殺，推允忠為帥。
units.en: In Xiantong 11 (870) He Quanhao was killed by his troops, who acclaimed Yunzhong as their commander.
units.literal: In Xiantong year eleven He Quanhao was killed by the army masses; they pushed Yunzhong as commander.

units.zh: 時僖宗為普王，即降詔遙領節度，授允忠左散騎常侍、兼御史中丞，充節度觀察留後。
units.en: Emperor Xizong was then Prince of Pu; he immediately issued an edict appointing Yunzhong Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Censor-in-Chief as acting military governor and observation commissioner.
units.literal: At the time Emperor Xizong was Prince of Pu; he immediately lowered an edict to hold the military governorship from afar, appointing Yunzhong Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, serving as military governor, observation commissioner, and acting regent.

units.zh: 不數月，轉檢校工部尚書、魏州大都督府長史、充魏博節度觀察等使。
units.en: Within a few months he was made Acting Minister of Works, chief administrator of Weizhou, and full military governor of Wei-Bo.
units.literal: Within several months he was transferred to Acting Minister of Works in the Ministry of Revenue, Chief Administrator of the Great Capital Prefecture of Weizhou, and military governor and observation commissioner of Wei-Bo.

units.zh: 累加至檢校司空、同平章事。
units.en: He rose in due course to Acting Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Councilor.
units.literal: By successive additions he reached Acting Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 乾符元年十一月卒，年六十一。
units.en: He died in the eleventh month of Qianfu 1 (874) at the age of sixty-one.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of Qianfu year one he died, age sixty-one.

units.zh: 累贈太尉。
units.en: He was posthumously promoted in stages to Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: By successive gifts he was made Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 子簡，自允忠初授戎帥，便為節度副使。
units.en: His son Jian had been made deputy military governor as soon as Yunzhong received his commission.
units.literal: His son Jian, from when Yunzhong was first given military command, was made military governor's deputy.

units.zh: 乾符初，累官至檢校工部尚書。
units.en: By the beginning of the Qianfu era he had risen to Acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianfu, by successive offices he reached Acting Minister of Works in the Ministry of Revenue.

units.zh: 允忠卒，即起復為節度觀察留後。
units.en: When Yunzhong died, Jian was immediately recalled from mourning to serve as acting military governor.
units.literal: When Yunzhong died, he was immediately recalled from mourning to be military governor, observation commissioner, and acting regent.

units.zh: 逾月，加檢校右僕射。
units.en: A month later he was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: After more than a month he was additionally made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 其後累加至侍中，封昌黎郡王。
units.en: He was subsequently promoted in stages to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as King of Changli.
units.literal: Thereafter by successive additions he reached Palace Attendant and was enfeoffed as King of Changli commandery.

units.zh: 賊巢之亂，諸葛爽受其偽命河陽節度使。
units.en: During Huang Chao's rebellion, Zhuge Shuang accepted a bogus appointment from him as military governor of Heyang.
units.literal: During the rebellion of the bandit Huang Chao, Zhuge Shuang received from him a false appointment as military governor of Heyang.

units.zh: 時僖宗在蜀，寇盜蜂起，簡據有六州，甲兵強盛，竊懷僭亂之志，且欲啟其封疆，乃舉兵攻河陽，爽棄城而走。
units.en: The emperor was then in Shu while rebels swarmed the land. Jian held six prefectures and a powerful army; nursing secret ambitions of rebellion and eager to enlarge his domain, he marched on Heyang, and Shuang abandoned the city and fled.
units.literal: At the time Emperor Xizong was in Shu; bandits and robbers swarmed forth. Jian held six prefectures, his armor and troops were strong, and he secretly harbored ambitions of usurpation and wished to expand his territory; he therefore raised troops to attack Heyang, and Shuang abandoned the city and fled.

units.zh: 簡遂留兵保守，因北掠邢、洺而歸，遂移軍攻鄆。
units.en: Jian left troops to hold Heyang, raided north through Xing and Ming, then turned his army against Yan.
units.literal: Jian then left troops to hold and defend the place, raided north through Xing and Ming and returned, then shifted his army to attack Yan.

units.zh: 鄆帥曹全晸出戰，爲簡所敗，死之。
units.en: Cao Quanzhen, governor of Yan, marched out to meet him, was defeated, and was killed.
units.literal: Cao Quanzhen, military governor of Yan, went out to battle and was defeated by Jian and killed.

units.zh: 鄆將崔君裕收合殘眾，保鄆州。
units.en: The Yan officer Cui Junyu rallied the survivors and held Yanzhou.
units.literal: The Yan general Cui Junyu gathered the scattered remnants and held Yan prefecture.

units.zh: 簡進攻其城，半年不下，河陽復爲諸葛爽所襲。
units.en: Jian besieged the city for half a year without success, while Heyang was seized again by Zhuge Shuang.
units.literal: Jian pressed the attack on the city for half a year without taking it; Heyang was again seized by Zhuge Shuang.

units.zh: 簡因欲先討君裕，次及河陽，乃舉兵至鄆，君裕請降。
units.en: Jian resolved to deal with Junyu first and Heyang afterward; he marched on Yan, and Junyu offered to surrender.
units.literal: Jian therefore wished first to subdue Junyu and afterward deal with Heyang; he raised troops and came to Yan, and Junyu requested surrender.

units.zh: 尋移軍復攻河陽，行及新鄕，爲爽軍逆擊，敗之。
units.en: He soon marched on Heyang again, but near Xinxing Shuang's troops met him head-on and routed him.
units.literal: Soon he shifted his army to attack Heyang again; when he reached Xinxing he was struck in counterattack by Shuang's army and defeated.

units.zh: 簡單騎奔回，憂憤。
units.en: Jian fled back alone on horseback, sick with grief and rage.
units.literal: Jian fled back alone on horseback, stricken with grief and anger.

units.zh: 疽發背而卒，時中和元年十一月也。
units.en: A carbuncle broke out between his shoulders and he died, in the eleventh month of the first year of Zhonghe.
units.literal: A carbuncle broke out on his back and he died — this was in the eleventh month of the first year of Zhonghe.

units.zh: 樂彥禎，魏州人也。
units.en: Le Yanzhen was a native of Weizhou.
units.literal: Le Yanzhen was a native of Weizhou.

units.zh: 父少寂，歷澶、博、貝三州刺史，贈工部尚書。
units.en: His father Shaoji had served as prefect of Chan, Bo, and Bei in turn and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
units.literal: His father Shaoji passed through the three prefectures of Chan, Bo, and Bei as prefect, and was posthumously given Minister of Works in the Ministry of Revenue.

units.zh: 彥禎少為本州軍校。
units.en: Yanzhen had been a regimental officer in the local army from youth.
units.literal: Yanzhen from youth was a military officer of the native prefecture.

units.zh: 韓簡之領節旄也，以彥禎為馬步軍都虞候，轉博州刺史。
units.en: When Han Jian took command, he made Yanzhen chief commandant of cavalry and infantry, then transferred him to prefect of Bo.
units.literal: When Han Jian received the commander's banner and staff, he made Yanzhen Chief Commandant of Cavalry and Infantry, then transferred him to prefect of Bo.

units.zh: 下河陽，走諸葛爽。
units.en: He attacked Heyang and drove off Zhuge Shuang.
units.literal: He descended on Heyang and drove off Zhuge Shuang.

units.zh: 有功，遷澶州刺史。
units.en: For this achievement he was transferred to prefect of Chan.
units.literal: For merit he was transferred to prefect of Chan.

units.zh: 簡再討河陽之敗也。
units.en: This was during Han Jian's second failed campaign against Heyang.
units.literal: This was when Jian again campaigned against Heyang and was defeated.

units.zh: 彥禎以一軍先歸，魏人遂共立之。
units.en: Yanzhen brought his division home first, and the Wei troops thereupon acclaimed him as their commander.
units.literal: Yanzhen with one army returned first; the Wei people thereupon jointly installed him.

units.zh: 朝廷尋授檢校工部尚書，知魏博留後。
units.en: The court soon appointed him Acting Minister of Works and acting regent of Wei-Bo.
units.literal: The court soon appointed him Acting Minister of Works and acting regent of Wei-Bo.

units.zh: 俄加戶部尚書，充節度觀察處置等使。
units.en: He was soon made Minister of Revenue and full military governor of Wei-Bo.
units.literal: Soon he was additionally made Minister of Revenue and military governor, observation commissioner, and disposition commissioner.

units.zh: 中和四年，累加至尚書左僕射、同平章事。
units.en: In Zhonghe 4 he rose in due course to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Grand Councilor.
units.literal: In Zhonghe year four he was by successive additions made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 僖宗自蜀回，加開府儀同三司，冊拜司徒。
units.en: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu, Yanzhen was made Grand General with Honorary Staff of Three Offices and ceremonially appointed Minister of Education.
units.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu he was additionally made Grand General with Honorary Staff of Three Offices and ceremonially appointed Minister of Education.

units.zh: 彥禎志滿驕大，動多不法。
units.en: Yanzhen grew arrogant and overbearing, and his conduct was often lawless.
units.literal: Yanzhen's ambition was full and he was arrogant and grand; his actions were often unlawful.

units.zh: 一旦征六州之眾，板築羅城，約河門舊堤，周八十里，月餘而畢，人用怨咨。
units.en: He once conscripted labor from all six prefectures to build an outer wall along the old Hemen dike, eighty li around. The work took just over a month, and the people groaned under the burden.
units.literal: One day he levied the masses of six prefectures, built ramparts for the outer wall, following the old dike at Hemen, eighty li in circumference; in a little more than a month it was completed, and the people murmured in resentment.

units.zh: 又其子從訓天資悖逆。
units.en: His son Congxun was by nature violent and rebellious.
units.literal: Moreover his son Congxun was by nature perverse and rebellious.

units.zh: 王鐸自滑移鎮滄州，過魏郊，從訓見其女妓，利之，先伏兵於漳南高雞泊，俟鐸之至，圍而害之，掠其所有。
units.en: When Wang Duo was transferred from Hua to Cangzhou and passed through Wei territory, Congxun saw his female entertainers and coveted them. He hid troops at Gaojipo south of Zhang, waited for Duo to arrive, surrounded and killed him, and plundered everything he had.
units.literal: Wang Duo shifted from Hua to command Cangzhou and passed through Wei's outskirts; Congxun saw his female entertainers and coveted them, first laying ambush troops at Gaojipo south of Zhang, waiting for Duo's arrival, surrounding and killing him, and plundering all he had.

units.zh: 時朝廷微弱，不能詰。
units.en: The court was too weak to hold him accountable.
units.literal: At the time the court was weak and could not investigate.

units.zh: 魏人素知鐸名望，議者惜之，而罪從訓。
units.en: The people of Wei had long respected Duo's standing; public opinion mourned him and condemned Congxun.
units.literal: The Wei people had long known Duo's reputation; commentators regretted it and blamed Congxun.

units.zh: 從訓又召亡命之徒五百餘輩，出入臥內，號為「子將」，委以腹心。
units.en: Congxun also gathered more than five hundred outlaws who came and went freely in his private quarters. He called them "son-generals" and treated them as his closest confidants.
units.literal: Congxun again summoned more than five hundred fugitive desperadoes to enter and leave his sleeping quarters, styled them "son-generals," and entrusted them with his innermost confidence.

units.zh: 軍人籍籍，各有異議。
units.en: The troops murmured among themselves, each faction nursing its own grievance.
units.literal: The military men murmured; each had differing views.

units.zh: 從訓聞而忌之，易服遁出，止於近縣。
units.en: When Congxun heard of this he grew suspicious, changed clothes, slipped out of the city, and lodged in a nearby county.
units.literal: Congxun heard and grew jealous; he changed clothes and slipped out, stopping at a nearby county.

units.zh: 彥禎因命為六州都指揮使。
units.en: Yanzhen then appointed him overall commander of the six prefectures.
units.literal: Yanzhen thereupon ordered him made overall commander of the six prefectures.

units.zh: 未幾，又兼相州刺史。
units.en: Before long he was also made prefect of Xiang.
units.literal: Before long he was additionally made prefect of Xiang.

units.zh: 到任之後，般輦軍器，取索錢帛，使人來往，交午塗路，軍府疑貳。
units.en: Once in office he shuttled weapons and extorted money and silk, sending couriers back and forth until the roads were crowded day and night. The headquarters grew suspicious and uneasy.
units.literal: After reaching his post he transported military equipment in relays, demanded money and silks, and sent men back and forth until the roads crossed at noon—the army headquarters grew doubtful and divided.

units.zh: 彥禎危憤而卒，眾推都將趙文㺹知留後事。
units.en: Yanzhen died in distress and anger. The troops acclaimed Chief Commander Zhao Wenkan to manage affairs as acting regent.
units.literal: Yanzhen died in peril and anger; the masses pushed Chief Commander Zhao Wenkan to manage acting regent affairs.

units.zh: 從訓自相州領兵三萬餘人至城下，文㺹按兵不出。
units.en: Congxun marched from Xiang with more than thirty thousand men and camped before the city. Wenkan held his troops inside and would not come out.
units.literal: Congxun from Xiang prefecture led more than thirty thousand troops to below the city walls; Wenkan held his troops and did not go out.

units.zh: 眾懷疑懼，復害文㺹，推羅弘信為帥。
units.en: The troops, fearful and suspicious, killed Wenkan in turn and acclaimed Luo Hongxin as their commander.
units.literal: The masses harbored doubt and fear, again killed Wenkan, and pushed Luo Hongxin as commander.

units.zh: 弘信以兵出戰，敗之。
units.en: Hongxin marched out to fight and defeated him.
units.literal: Hongxin led troops out to battle and defeated him.

units.zh: 從訓招集餘眾，次於洹水。
units.en: Congxun rallied his remaining forces and encamped on the Huan River.
units.literal: Congxun gathered the remaining masses and encamped at Huan River.

units.zh: 弘信遣將程公佐領兵討擊，大敗之，梟從訓首於軍門，時文德元年春也。
units.en: Hongxin sent the general Cheng Gongzuo against him, routed his army, and displayed Congxun's head at the camp gate. This was in the spring of Wende 1.
units.literal: Hongxin dispatched the general Cheng Gongzuo to lead troops in pursuit and attack, greatly defeated him, and displayed Congxun's head at the army gates—it was spring of Wende year one.

units.zh: 羅弘信，字德孚，魏州貴鄉人。
units.en: Luo Hongxin, courtesy name Defu, was a native of Guixiang in Weizhou.
units.literal: Luo Hongxin, style Defu, was a native of Guixiang in Weizhou.

units.zh: 曾祖秀，祖珍，父讓，皆為本州軍校。
units.en: His great-grandfather Xiu, grandfather Zhen, and father Rang had all been military officers in the local army.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Xiu, grandfather Zhen, and father Rang were all military officers of the native prefecture.

units.zh: 弘信少從戎役，歷事節度使韓簡、樂彥禎。
units.en: Hongxin entered military service young and served under the military governors Han Jian and Le Yanzhen.
units.literal: Hongxin from youth followed military service and successively served military governors Han Jian and Le Yanzhen.

units.zh: 光啟末，彥禎子從訓忌牙軍，出居於外，軍眾廢彥禎，推趙文㺹權主軍州事。
units.en: At the end of the Guangqi era, Yanzhen's son Congxun, fearing the yamen guard, moved outside the city. The troops deposed Yanzhen and put Zhao Wenkan in charge of military and civil affairs.
units.literal: At the end of Guangqi, Yanzhen's son Congxun feared the yamen guard army, went out to reside elsewhere, the army masses deposed Yanzhen, and pushed Zhao Wenkan to hold military and prefectural affairs in authority.

units.zh: 眾復以為不便，因推弘信為帥。
units.en: The troops soon found this arrangement unsatisfactory and acclaimed Hongxin as their commander instead.
units.literal: The masses again thought this inconvenient and therefore pushed Hongxin as commander.

units.zh: 先是，有鄰人密謂弘信曰：「某嘗夜遇一白鬚翁，相告雲，君當為土地主。
units.en: Earlier a neighbor had told Hongxin in secret, "One night I met a white-bearded old man who said to me, 'Your neighbor shall be lord of this land.
units.literal: Earlier a neighbor secretly told Hongxin: "I once at night met a white-bearded old man who told me, saying, 'You shall be lord of this land.

units.zh: 如是者再三。」
units.en: This happened again and again.'"
units.literal: It was like this three or four times.'"

units.zh: 弘信竊異之。
units.en: Hongxin had privately wondered at this.
units.literal: Hongxin privately marveled at this.

units.zh: 及廢文㺹，軍人聚呼曰：「孰願為節度使者？」
units.en: When Wenkan was removed, the soldiers gathered and shouted, "Who will be military governor?"
units.literal: When Wenkan was deposed the military men gathered and shouted: "Who wishes to be military governor?"

units.zh: 弘信即應之曰：「白鬚翁早以命我。」
units.en: Hongxin answered at once, "The white-bearded old man long ago destined me for it."
units.literal: Hongxin at once responded: "The white-bearded old man long ago commanded me."

units.zh: 眾乃環而視之，曰：「可也。」
units.en: The men surrounded him and said, "He will do."
units.literal: The masses then encircled and looked at him, saying: "He will do."

units.zh: 由是立之。
units.en: On that basis they installed him.
units.literal: Thereby he was installed.

units.zh: 僖宗聞之，文德元年四月，詔加工部尚書，權知節度留後。
units.en: When Emperor Xizong learned of this, in the fourth month of Wende 1 he was made Minister of Works and acting military governor.
units.literal: Emperor Xizong heard of it; in the fourth month of Wende year one an edict additionally made him Minister of Works and acting military governor regent.

units.zh: 七月，復加金紫光祿大夫、檢校尚書右僕射，充魏博節度觀察處置等使。
units.en: In the seventh month he was made Golden-Gleam Glory Grand Master, Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and full military governor of Wei-Bo.
units.literal: In the seventh month he was again given Golden-Gleam Glory Grand Master and Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, serving as Wei-Bo military governor, observation commissioner, and disposition commissioner.

units.zh: 龍紀中，加檢校司空、同平章事，封豫章郡公。
units.en: During the Longji era he was made Acting Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Councilor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuzhang.
units.literal: In the Longji reign he was additionally made Acting Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Councilor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuzhang commandery.

units.zh: 乾寧中，朱全忠急攻兗鄆，朱瑄求援於太原。
units.en: During the Qianning era Zhu Quanzhong pressed his attack on Yan and Yanzhou, and Zhu Xuan sought help from Taiyuan.
units.literal: In the Qianning reign Zhu Quanzhong urgently attacked Yan and Yanzhou; Zhu Xuan sought aid from Taiyuan.

units.zh: 太原發軍，假道於魏，令大將李存信屯莘縣。
units.en: Taiyuan sent an army through Wei by permission and stationed the great general Li Cunxin at Shen county.
units.literal: Taiyuan dispatched troops, borrowing passage through Wei, and ordered the great general Li Cunxin to encamp at Shen county.

units.zh: 存信御軍無法，侵魏之芻牧，弘信不平之。
units.en: Cunxin disciplined his troops poorly and encroached on Wei's fodder and pastures. Hongxin resented this.
units.literal: Cunxin commanded the army without discipline, encroaching on Wei's fodder and pastures; Hongxin was displeased.

units.zh: 全忠復遣人謂之曰：「太原志吞河朔，回戈之日，貴道堪憂。」
units.en: Quanzhong sent another envoy to warn him, "Taiyuan means to swallow all of Hebei. When they turn their spears homeward, your circuit will be in peril."
units.literal: Quanzhong again sent a man to tell him: "Taiyuan intends to swallow Hebei; on the day they turn their spears back, your honored circuit will be cause for worry."

units.zh: 弘信乃托好於汴，出師三萬攻存信，敗之。
units.en: Hongxin then feigned friendship with Bian, marched thirty thousand men against Cunxin, and defeated him.
units.literal: Hongxin thereupon pretended friendship with Bian, marched out thirty thousand to attack Cunxin, and defeated him.

units.zh: 太原怒，舉兵攻魏，營於觀音門外。
units.en: Taiyuan was furious and marched on Wei, encamping outside Guanyin Gate.
units.literal: Taiyuan was enraged, raised troops to attack Wei, and encamped outside Guanyin Gate.

units.zh: 汴將葛從周援之，屯於洹水。
units.en: Ge Congzhou of Bian came to his aid and encamped on the Huan River.
units.literal: Bian's general Ge Congzhou came to aid him and encamped at Huan River.

units.zh: 李克用子落落時為鐵林軍使，為從周所擒，乃退歸。
units.en: Li Keyong's son Luoluo, then commander of the Iron Forest Army, was captured by Congzhou, and the Taiyuan army withdrew.
units.literal: Li Keyong's son Luoluo at the time was Iron Forest Army commissioner; he was captured by Congzhou, and they then withdrew and returned.

units.zh: 自是太原之師，每歲侵擾相、魏，魏人患之。
units.en: Thereafter the Taiyuan army raided Xiang and Wei year after year, to the great distress of the Wei people.
units.literal: From this the Taiyuan army every year harassed Xiang and Wei; the Wei people suffered from it.

units.zh: 硃全忠方事兗鄆，懼弘信離貳，每歲時賂遺，必卑辭厚禮答貺。
units.en: Quanzhong was then occupied with Yan and Yanzhou and feared Hongxin might turn against him. Every year he sent gifts, and Hongxin always replied with humble words and lavish courtesy.
units.literal: Zhu Quanzhong was then engaged with Yan and Yanzhou, feared Hongxin would turn disloyal, and every year at the seasons sent gifts; Hongxin always answered with humble words and generous courtesy in return.

units.zh: 全忠對魏使北面拜而受之，曰：「六兄比予倍年已上，兄弟之國，安得以常鄰遇之。」
units.en: Quanzhong would bow northward to Wei's envoy as he received the gifts, saying, "Sixth Elder Brother is more than twice my age. As brother states, how can we treat each other as ordinary neighbors?"
units.literal: Quanzhong toward Wei's envoy bowed facing north and received it, saying: "Sixth Elder Brother is more than twice my years; as brother states, how can we be treated as ordinary neighbors?"

units.zh: 弘信以為厚己，亦推心焉。
units.en: Hongxin took this as genuine regard for himself and gave Quanzhong his trust in return.
units.literal: Hongxin thought this showed generosity toward himself and also gave his heart in return.

units.zh: 弘信累官至檢校太師、守侍中、臨清王。
units.en: Hongxin rose in due course to Acting Grand Preceptor, Guardian Palace Attendant, and King of Linqing.
units.literal: Hongxin by successive offices reached Acting Grand Preceptor, Guardian Palace Attendant, and King of Linqing.

units.zh: 光化元年九月卒，年六十三，贈太師，追封北平王，謚曰莊肅。
units.en: He died in the ninth month of Guanghua 1 at the age of sixty-three. He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as King of Northern Ping, and given the posthumous title Zhuangsu.
units.literal: In the ninth month of Guanghua year one he died, age sixty-three; posthumously given Grand Preceptor, posthumously enfeoffed as King of Northern Ping, posthumous title Zhuangsu.

units.zh: 子威。
units.en: His son was Wei.
units.literal: His son Wei.

units.zh: 威，字端己。
units.en: Wei, courtesy name Duanji.
units.literal: Wei, style Duanji.

units.zh: 文德初，授左散騎常侍，充天雄軍節度副使。
units.en: At the beginning of the Wende era he was appointed Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and deputy military governor of the Tianxiong Army.
units.literal: At the beginning of Wende he was appointed Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and served as deputy military governor of the Tianxiong Army.

units.zh: 自龍紀至乾寧，十年之中，累加官爵。
units.en: From the Longji through the Qianning eras, he accumulated offices and titles over ten years.
units.literal: From Longji to Qianning, within ten years he was by successive additions given offices and ranks.

units.zh: 弘信卒，襲父位為留後，朝廷從而命之。
units.en: When Hongxin died, Wei succeeded him as acting regent, and the court confirmed the appointment.
units.literal: When Hongxin died he succeeded to his father's position as acting regent; the court followed and appointed him.

units.zh: 天復末，累加至檢校太傅、兼侍中、長沙王。
units.en: By the end of the Tianfu era he had risen to Acting Grand Tutor, concurrent Palace Attendant, and King of Changsha.
units.literal: At the end of Tianfu he was by successive additions made Acting Grand Tutor, concurrent Palace Attendant, and King of Changsha.

units.zh: 天祐初，授檢校太尉、守侍中，進封鄴王，賜號「忠勤宣力致理功臣」。
units.en: Early in the Tianyou era he was made Acting Grand Commandant and Guardian Palace Attendant, promoted to King of Ye, and granted the title "Meritorious Minister of Loyal Diligence, Proclaiming Power, and Ordering Governance."
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou he was appointed Acting Grand Commandant, Guardian Palace Attendant, advanced to King of Ye, and granted the title "Meritorious Minister of Loyal Diligence, Proclaiming Power, and Ordering Governance."

units.zh: 魏之牙中軍者，自至德中，田承嗣盜據相、魏、澶、博、衛、貝等六州，召募軍中子弟置之部下，遂以為號。
units.en: Wei's yamen guard army dated from the Zhide era, when Tian Chengsi seized Xiang, Wei, Chan, Bo, Wei, and Bei and the other six prefectures. He enrolled soldiers' sons and younger brothers in his personal following, and they took that as their name.
units.literal: Wei's yamen guard army: from the Zhide reign Tian Chengsi by stealth held Xiang, Wei, Chan, Bo, Wei, and Bei and other six prefectures, recruited army sons and younger brothers and placed them under his command, and thereby made it their title.

units.zh: 皆豐給厚賜，不勝驕寵。
units.en: They were lavishly paid and rewarded until pride and indulgence knew no bounds.
units.literal: All were richly supplied and generously rewarded, beyond bearing in pride and favor.

units.zh: 年代浸遠，父子相襲，親黨膠固。
units.en: As generations passed, fathers and sons succeeded one another in the ranks, and kinship ties grew iron-hard.
units.literal: As years gradually lengthened, fathers and sons succeeded one another, kin and partisans bonded solid.

units.zh: 其凶戾者，強買豪奪，逾法犯令，長吏不能禁。
units.en: The most violent among them extorted goods by force, broke the law with impunity, and local officials could not restrain them.
units.literal: The fierce and cruel among them forcibly bought and seized by force, exceeded the law and violated orders, and senior officials could not prohibit them.

units.zh: 變易主帥，有同兒戲，如史憲誠、何進滔、韓君雄、樂彥禎，皆為其所立。
units.en: Replacing commanders was child's play to them. Shi Xiancheng, He Jintao, Han Junxiong, and Le Yanzhen had all been installed by the guard.
units.literal: Changing commanders was like child's play; such as Shi Xiancheng, He Jintao, Han Junxiong, and Le Yanzhen were all installed by them.

units.zh: 優獎小不如意，則舉族被害。
units.en: If rewards fell the least bit short of their expectations, entire clans were slaughtered.
units.literal: If favors and rewards were slightly not to their liking, then the whole clan was harmed.

units.zh: 威懲其往弊，雖以貨賂姑息，而心銜之。
units.en: Wei was determined to end these abuses. Though he placated the guard with gifts and bribes, he nursed a deep grievance against them.
units.literal: Wei punished their past abuses; though he used goods and bribes to indulge them, in his heart he harbored resentment.

units.zh: 威嗣世之明年，正月，幽州劉仁恭擁兵十萬，謀亂河朔，進陷貝州，長驅攻魏。
units.en: In the first month of the year after Wei succeeded his father, Liu Rengong of Youzhou marched a hundred thousand men to stir trouble in Hebei, seized Bei prefecture, and drove straight at Wei.
units.literal: In the year after Wei succeeded to his line, in the first month, Youzhou's Liu Rengong held a hundred thousand troops, plotted disorder in Hebei, advanced and took Bei prefecture, and drove straight to attack Wei.

units.zh: 威求援於汴。
units.en: Wei sought help from Bian.
units.literal: Wei sought aid from Bian.

units.zh: 硃全忠遣將李思安屯於洹水。
units.en: Zhu Quanzhong sent the general Li Si'an to encamp on the Huan River.
units.literal: Zhu Quanzhong dispatched the general Li Si'an to encamp at Huan River.

units.zh: 葛從周自邢、洺引軍入魏。
units.en: Ge Congzhou marched from Xing and Ming into Wei.
units.literal: Ge Congzhou from Xing and Ming led troops into Wei.

units.zh: 燕將劉守文、單可及攻汴軍於內黃。
units.en: The Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keji attacked the Bian army at Neihuang.
units.literal: Yan's generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keji attacked Bian's army at Neihuang.

units.zh: 思安逆戰，大敗之，乘勝追躡。
units.en: Si'an met them in battle, routed them, and pursued the fleeing army.
units.literal: Si'an met them in battle and greatly defeated them, riding victory in pursuit.

units.zh: 從周出會掩擊，覆敗燕軍，斬首三萬。
units.en: Congzhou came out to join the attack from ambush, crushed the Yan army, and took thirty thousand heads.
units.literal: Congzhou came out to join in a concealed strike, overthrew and defeated the Yan army, and beheaded thirty thousand.

units.zh: 三年，威引汴軍攻滄州以報之。
units.en: In the third year Wei led Bian troops against Cangzhou in retaliation.
units.literal: In year three Wei led Bian troops to attack Cangzhou in retaliation.

units.zh: 自是，威感全忠援助之恩，合從景附。
units.en: From then on Wei was grateful for Quanzhong's aid and drew ever closer to him in alliance.
units.literal: From this Wei felt Quanzhong's grace in aiding him and joined in alliance and drew close in attachment.

units.zh: 天祐二年七月十三日夜，牙軍裨校李公佺作亂，威僅以身免。
units.en: On the night of the thirteenth day of the seventh month of Tianyou 2, yamen guard deputy Li Gongquan mutinied, and Wei barely escaped with his life.
units.literal: On the night of the thirteenth day of the seventh month of Tianyou year two, yamen guard army deputy commander Li Gongquan made disorder; Wei barely escaped with his person.

units.zh: 公佺出奔滄州。
units.en: Gongquan fled to Cangzhou.
units.literal: Gongquan fled out to Cangzhou.

units.zh: 自是愈懼，遣使求援於全忠，密謀破之。
units.en: Wei grew still more fearful and sent envoys to Quanzhong for aid, secretly plotting to destroy the guard.
units.literal: From this he grew ever more fearful, dispatched envoys to seek aid from Quanzhong, and secretly plotted to destroy them.

units.zh: 全忠遣李思安會魏博軍，再攻滄州。
units.en: Quanzhong sent Li Si'an with Wei-Bo troops to attack Cangzhou again.
units.literal: Quanzhong dispatched Li Si'an to join Wei-Bo troops and again attack Cangzhou.

units.zh: 全忠女妻威子廷規，先是卒。
units.en: Quanzhong's daughter had been married to Wei's son Tinggui; she had earlier died.
units.literal: Quanzhong's daughter had married Wei's son Tinggui; she had earlier died.

units.zh: 全忠遣長直軍校馬嗣勳選兵千人，密於輿中實兵甲入魏，言助女葬事。
units.en: Quanzhong sent the long-service officer Ma Sixun with a thousand picked men, weapons hidden in funeral carts, under the pretext of attending his daughter's burial in Wei.
units.literal: Quanzhong dispatched the long-service direct army officer Ma Sixun to select a thousand troops, secretly filling carriages with armor and weapons to enter Wei, saying it was to assist with the daughter's funeral.

units.zh: 三年正月五日，嗣勳至，全忠親率大軍濟河，言視行營於滄景。
units.en: On the fifth day of the first month of the third year Sixun arrived, and Quanzhong personally led a great army across the river, claiming he was inspecting the Cangjing front.
units.literal: On the fifth day of the first month of year three Sixun arrived; Quanzhong personally led a great army across the river, saying he was inspecting the camp at Cangjing.

units.zh: 威欲因而出迎，至期，即假全忠帳下銳卒入而夾攻之。
units.en: Wei planned to go out to welcome him and, when the day came, let Quanzhong's elite troops into the city to attack the guard from both sides.
units.literal: Wei wished thereby to go out to welcome him; when the day came he would borrow Quanzhong's sharp troops from under his tent to enter and strike them from both sides.

units.zh: 牙軍頗疑，堅請不出。
units.en: The guard grew suspicious and insisted he stay inside.
units.literal: The yamen guard army was quite suspicious and firmly begged that he not go out.

units.zh: 威恐洩其事，慰納之。
units.en: Fearing his plot would leak out, Wei soothed them and agreed to stay.
units.literal: Wei feared the matter would leak and comforted and accepted them.

units.zh: 是月十四日夜，率廝養百十輩，與嗣勳合攻之。
units.en: On the night of the fourteenth he led a hundred-odd personal retainers and joined Sixun in the attack.
units.literal: On the night of the fourteenth day of that month he led a hundred-odd personal attendants and together with Sixun attacked them.

units.zh: 時宿於牙城者千人，遲明殺之殆盡；
units.en: By dawn nearly all of the thousand men quartered in the yamen city had been killed;
units.literal: At the time a thousand lodging in the yamen city were by dawn killed nearly to the last;

units.zh: 凡八千家，皆破其族。
units.en: eight thousand households in all had their entire clans wiped out.
units.literal: in all eight thousand households, all their clans were destroyed.

units.zh: 魏軍攻滄州者，在歷亭聞有變，其將史仁遇擁之，保於高唐。
units.en: The Wei troops besieging Cangzhou, encamped at Liting, heard of the upheaval. Their commander Shi Renyu held them together and withdrew to Gaotang.
units.literal: The Wei troops attacking Cangzhou, at Liting hearing there was a change, their general Shi Renyu held them and defended at Gaotang.

units.zh: 六州之內，皆為讎敵，累月平之。
units.en: Throughout the six prefectures every survivor became an enemy, and it took months to pacify the region.
units.literal: Within the six prefectures all became enemies; over many months it was pacified.

units.zh: 威仕梁數年後卒，年三十四，位至守太師、兼中書令，贈尚書令，謚曰貞壯。
units.en: Wei served the Liang court for several years and died at thirty-four, having reached Guardian Grand Preceptor and concurrent Chief Minister of the Secretariat. He was posthumously made Director of the Department of State Affairs with the posthumous title Zhenzhuang.
units.literal: Wei served Liang several years then died, age thirty-four; his position reached Guardian Grand Preceptor and concurrent Chief Minister of the Secretariat; posthumously given Director of the Department of State Affairs; posthumous title Zhenzhuang.

units.zh: 威性明敏，達於吏道。
units.en: Wei was intelligent and quick-witted and skilled in administration.
units.literal: Wei's nature was bright and keen; he was accomplished in the ways of officials.

units.zh: 伏膺儒術，招納文人，聚書至萬卷。
units.en: He revered Confucian learning, gathered scholars about him, and amassed a library of ten thousand scrolls.
units.literal: He bowed to Confucian learning, recruited literary men, and gathered books to ten thousand scrolls.

units.zh: 每花朝月夕，與賓佐賦詠，甚有情致。
units.en: On spring days and moonlit nights he would compose poetry with his staff, with real grace and feeling.
units.literal: Every flower morning and moon evening he composed poetry with guests and aides, with very much feeling and charm.

units.zh: 錢塘人羅隱者，有當世詩名，自號「江東生」。
units.en: Luo Yin of Qiantang enjoyed great renown as a poet of his day and styled himself "Eastern River Student."
units.literal: The man of Qiantang Luo Yin had contemporary poetic fame and styled himself "Eastern River Student."

units.zh: 威遣使賂遺，敘其宗姓，推為叔父。
units.en: Wei sent envoys with gifts, traced their shared clan ancestry, and treated Yin as his uncle.
units.literal: Wei dispatched envoys with gifts, set forth their clan surnames, and honored him as paternal uncle.

units.zh: 隱亦集其詩寄之。
units.en: Yin in turn sent Wei a collection of his poems.
units.literal: Yin also collected his poems and sent them to him.

units.zh: 威酷嗜其作，目己所為曰《偷江東集》，凡五卷，今鄴中人士諷詠之。
units.en: Wei adored his work and titled his own compositions Collected Poems Pilfered from the Eastern River, five scrolls in all. They are still recited among the gentry of Ye.
units.literal: Wei intensely loved his writings, titled his own compositions Collected Poems Pilfered from the Eastern River, five scrolls in all; now people of Ye recite and chant them.

units.zh: 史臣曰：魏、鎮、燕三鎮，不能制之也久矣。
units.en: The historiographer comments: The court has long been unable to control the three commands of Wei, Zhen, and Yan.
units.literal: The historiographer says: The three commands of Wei, Zhen, and Yan—the court has long been unable to control them.

units.zh: 兵強地廣，合從連衡。
units.en: Their armies were strong and their territories vast; they formed alliances and played the balance of power.
units.literal: Troops strong and territory broad, they joined in alliance and linked in balance of power.

units.zh: 爵命雖假於朝廷，群臣自謀於元帥。
units.en: Though titles came from the court on paper, the ministers plotted with their own commanders.
units.literal: Titles and appointments though borrowed from the court, the ministers themselves plotted with the commander-in-chief.

units.zh: 如史憲誠等五家，其初皆因此而得之，其後亦因此而失之。
units.en: The five houses represented here, beginning with Shi Xiancheng, all gained their power in this way—and lost it in the same way.
units.literal: Such as the five houses of Shi Xiancheng and others—at first all gained power thereby, and afterward also lost it thereby.

units.zh: 蓋不知取之以權，守之以仁，則遠矣。
units.en: They did not understand that power seized by force must be held by benevolence; without that wisdom, ruin was inevitable.
units.literal: For they did not know to take power by expedient means and hold it by benevolence—then they would have been far from ruin.

units.zh: 若善繼者，史氏、羅氏之二子有焉，其餘不足觀也。
units.en: Among those who governed well, only the sons of the Shi and Luo families qualify; the rest are hardly worth notice.
units.literal: As for those who succeeded well, the two sons of the Shi and Luo clans had it; the rest are not worth viewing.

units.zh: 贊曰：逆取順守，古亦有之。
units.en: Eulogy: Seizing power by force yet ruling with obedience to the throne—history offers precedents even for that.
units.literal: The eulogy says: Taking power by rebellion and holding it by obedience—antiquity also had such cases.

units.zh: 如其逆守，滅亡必隨。
units.en: But to seize power by rebellion and cling to it by rebellion is to invite certain ruin.
units.literal: If one holds power by rebellion, destruction and extinction must follow.

units.zh: 史、何、韓、樂，世數盛衰。
units.en: The houses of Shi, He, Han, and Le rose and fell across the generations.
units.literal: Shi, He, Han, and Le—generations counted in rise and fall.

units.zh: 足以為鑒，念茲在茲。
units.en: Let their fate be a warning—let this lesson never be forgotten.
units.literal: Sufficient to serve as a mirror; keep this ever in mind.

units.zh: 燕將劉守文、單可及攻汴軍於內黃。
units.en: The Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keyi attacked the Bian forces at Neihuang.
units.literal: The Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keyi attacked the Bian army at Neihuang.

units.zh: 初，樞自歙州罷郡歸朝，路經大梁，時硃全忠兵威已振，樞以兄事之，全忠由是重之。
units.en: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.
units.literal: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.

units.zh: 制出，硃全忠保薦之，言樞有經世才，不可棄之嶺表，尋復拜門下侍郎，監修國史，累兼吏部尚書，判度支。
units.en: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed vice minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as minister of personnel, administering the treasury.
units.literal: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as Minister of Personnel, administering the treasury.

units.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。
units.en: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.
units.literal: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。
units.en: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。
units.en: After Cui Yin's execution, Shu's ties to Quanzhong kept him in the chancellorship unchanged.
units.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because of his longstanding closeness to Quanzhong Shu's chancellorship remained unchanged.

units.zh: 汴將葛從周援之，屯於洹水。
units.en: Ge Congzhou of Bian came to his relief and encamped on the Huan River.
units.literal: The Bian general Ge Congzhou came to his aid and encamped at the Huan River.

units.zh: 李克用子落落時爲鐵林軍使，爲從周所擒，乃退歸。
units.en: Li Keyong's son Luoluo, then commander of the Iron Forest Army, was captured by Congzhou, and Taiyuan withdrew.
units.literal: Li Keyong's son Luoluo was then Iron Forest Army commander; he was captured by Congzhou and Taiyuan then withdrew.

units.zh: 葛從周自邢、洺引軍入魏。
units.en: Ge Congzhou marched in from Xing and Ming.
units.literal: Ge Congzhou led troops from Xing and Ming into Wei.

units.zh: 從周出會掩擊，覆敗燕軍，斬首三萬。
units.en: Congzhou came out to strike in concert, crushed the Yan army, and took thirty thousand heads.
units.literal: Congzhou came out to join in a converging strike and annihilated the Yan army, beheading thirty thousand.

units.zh: 全忠遣長直軍校馬嗣勳選兵千人，密於輿中實兵甲入魏，言助女葬事。
units.en: Quanzhong sent Ma Cixun of the long-service guard to choose a thousand men and smuggle arms into Wei in funeral litters, under the pretext of helping bury his daughter.
units.literal: Quanzhong sent the chief of the long-service guard Ma Cixun to select a thousand troops; arms and armor were secretly loaded in the palanquins that entered Wei, on the pretext of assisting with the daughter's funeral.

units.zh: 三年正月五日，嗣勳至，全忠親率大軍濟河，言視行營於滄景。
units.en: On the fifth day of the first month in the third year Cixun arrived; Quanzhong himself led a great army across the river, saying he meant to inspect the Cangjing front.
units.literal: On the fifth day of the first month of the third year Cixun arrived; Quanzhong personally led a great army across the river, saying he was going to inspect the camp at Cangjing.

units.zh: 是月十四日夜，率廝養百十輩，與嗣勳合攻之。
units.en: On the night of the fourteenth he led a hundred-odd personal retainers to join Cixun in the assault.
units.literal: On the night of the fourteenth day of that month he led a hundred or so personal attendants to join Cixun in a combined attack.

units.zh: 唐興，因隋樂不改，及黃巢之亂，樂縣散失，太常博士殷盈孫以周法鑄穀鐘、編鐘，處士蕭承訓等校石磐，合而奏之。
units.en: When the Tang rose, they retained Sui music unchanged. During Huang Chao's rebellion the court instruments were scattered and lost. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun recast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, while the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others retuned stone chimes, and the restored ensemble was played together once more.
units.literal: When the Tang rose, they took over Sui music without change; at the turmoil of Huang Chao the musical stands were scattered and lost; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun cast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, and the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others tuned stone chimes, and together they were played.

units.zh: 眾懷疑懼，復害文㺹，推羅弘信爲帥。
units.en: The army grew fearful and restless; they killed Wenqing in turn and set up Luo Hongxin as commander.
units.literal: The masses were suspicious and afraid; they again killed Wenqing and pushed Luo Hongxin forward as commander.

units.zh: 羅弘信，字德孚，魏州貴鄕人。
units.en: Luo Hongxin, styled Defu, came from Guixiang in Weizhou.
units.literal: Luo Hongxin, styled Defu, was a man of Guixiang in Weizhou.

units.zh: 光化元年九月卒，年六十三，贈太師，追封北平王，謚曰莊肅。
units.en: He died in the ninth month of the first year of Guanghua at sixty-three; the court posthumously made him Grand Preceptor, Prince of Beiping, with the posthumous title Zhuangsu.
units.literal: He died in the ninth month of the first year of Guanghua, aged sixty-three; posthumously he was made Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping, and given the posthumous title Zhuangsu.

units.zh: 弘信累官至檢校太師、守侍中、臨清王。
units.en: Hongxin rose in time to Acting Grand Preceptor, Defender Palace Attendant, and Prince of Linqing.
units.literal: Hongxin rose in office to Acting Grand Preceptor, Defender Palace Attendant, and Prince of Linqing.

units.zh: 龍紀中，加檢校司空、同平章事，封豫章郡公。
units.en: During the Longji reign he was made Acting Grand Minister of Works, Concurrent Grand Councilor, and Duke of Yuzhang.
units.literal: In the Longji era he was added Acting Grand Minister of Works, Concurrent Grand Councilor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuzhang commandery.

units.zh: 七月，復加金紫光祿大夫、檢校尚書右僕射，充魏博節度觀察處置等使。
units.en: In the seventh month he was further made Golden-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and military governor, observation commissioner, and disposition commissioner of Weibo.
units.literal: In the seventh month he was again added Golden-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Military Governor, Observation Commissioner, and Disposition Commissioner of Weibo.

units.zh: 弘信少從戎役，歷事節度使韓簡、樂彥禎。
units.en: Hongxin entered military service young and served in turn under Han Jian and Le Yanzhen.
units.literal: In youth Hongxin followed military service and successively served the military governors Han Jian and Le Yanzhen.

units.zh: 子威。
units.en: His son was Wei.
units.literal: His son was Wei.

units.zh: 弘信子 威威，字端己。
units.en: Hongxin's son Wei, styled Duanji.
units.literal: Hongxin's son Wei — Wei, styled Duanji.

units.zh: 僖宗聞之，文德元年四月，詔加工部尚書，權知節度留後。
units.en: When Emperor Xizong learned of it, in the fourth month of the first year of Wende he was made Minister of Public Works and authorized as acting military governor.
units.literal: When Emperor Xizong heard of this, in the fourth month of the first year of Wende an edict added the post of Minister of Works and authorized him to act as Acting Military Governor.

units.zh: 弘信乃托好於汴，出師三萬攻存信，敗之。
units.en: Hongxin therefore courted Bian, marched out thirty thousand men against Cunxin, and defeated him.
units.literal: Hongxin therefore made a show of friendship with Bian and marched out thirty thousand men to attack Cunxin and defeated him.

units.zh: 弘信以爲厚己，亦推心焉。
units.en: Hongxin took this as genuine regard and gave Quanzhong his full trust in return.
units.literal: Hongxin thought he was treating him generously and also gave him his full trust.

units.zh: 弘信即應之曰：「白鬚翁早以命我。」
units.en: Hongxin answered at once, "The white-bearded old man appointed me long ago."
units.literal: Hongxin immediately answered: "The white-bearded old man long ago commanded me."

units.zh: 弘信以兵出戰，敗之。
units.en: Hongxin took the field and defeated him.
units.literal: Hongxin went out to battle with troops and defeated him.

units.zh: 弘信遣將程公佐領兵討擊，大敗之，梟從訓首於軍門，時文德元年春也。
units.en: Hongxin sent Cheng Gongzuo in pursuit, routed him utterly, and displayed Congxun's head before the army gate in the spring of the first year of Wende.
units.literal: Hongxin sent the general Cheng Gongzuo to lead troops in pursuit and attack; he inflicted a great defeat and displayed Congxun's head at the army gate — this was in the spring of the first year of Wende.

units.zh: 眾復以爲不便，因推弘信爲帥。
units.en: The troops soon found this arrangement unsatisfactory and set up Hongxin instead.
units.literal: The masses again found this unsuitable and therefore pushed Hongxin forward as commander.

units.zh: 先是，有鄰人密謂弘信曰：「某嘗夜遇一白鬚翁，相告雲，君當爲土地主。
units.en: Earlier a neighbor had told him in private, "One night I met a white-bearded old man who said you would become lord of this land.
units.literal: Earlier a neighbor had secretly told Hongxin: "I once met a white-bearded old man at night who told me that you would become master of the land.

units.zh: 弘信竊異之。
units.en: Hongxin kept the story to himself and wondered at it.
units.literal: Hongxin secretly marveled at this.

units.zh: 存信御軍無法，侵魏之芻牧，弘信不平之。
units.en: Cunxin kept poor discipline and plundered Wei's fodder and pasture, to Hongxin's anger.
units.literal: Cunxin governed his troops without discipline and encroached on Wei's fodder and pasture; Hongxin was displeased.

units.zh: 朱全忠方事兗鄆，懼弘信離貳，每歲時賂遺，必卑辭厚禮答貺。
units.en: Quanzhong was then busy with Yan and Yun and feared Hongxin might waver; every season he sent gifts, and Hongxin always replied with humble words and lavish return gifts.
units.literal: Zhu Quanzhong was then engaged with Yan and Yun and feared that Hongxin might turn aside; every year at the seasons he sent gifts, and Hongxin always answered with humble words and generous return gifts.

units.zh: 全忠對魏使北面拜而受之，曰：「六兄比予倍年已上，兄弟之國，安得以常鄰遇之。」
units.en: Quanzhong would face north and bow to receive Wei's gifts, saying, "Sixth Brother is more than twice my age; we are brothers in arms — how could I treat him as an ordinary neighbor?"
units.literal: Quanzhong, facing Wei's envoy, bowed toward the north to receive the gifts and said: "Sixth Brother is more than twice my age; we are a state of brothers — how can I treat him as an ordinary neighbor?"

units.zh: 弘信卒，襲父位爲留後，朝廷從而命之。
units.en: When Hongxin died, Wei succeeded as acting governor, and the court confirmed the appointment.
units.literal: When Hongxin died, Wei succeeded to his father's post as acting governor, and the court accordingly appointed him.

units.zh: 事未行，會赦王廷湊，諸道班師。
units.en: Before the plan could be enacted, Wang Tingcou was pardoned and the allied armies withdrew.
units.literal: Before the matter could be carried out, there came an amnesty for Wang Tingcou; the various circuits withdrew their armies.

units.zh: 初，同捷狂桀犯命，濟之以王廷湊，王師經年無功。
units.en: At first Tongjie's wild defiance of orders was sustained by aid from Wang Tingcou, and the imperial armies had failed for years.
units.literal: At first Tongjie was wild and defiant in offending orders; he was aided by Wang Tingcou; the imperial army for years had no success.

units.zh: 中和末，以太原李克用兵勢方盛，與定州王處存密相締結。
units.en: Late in the Zhonghe era, fearing the rising power of Li Keyong of Taiyuan, Keju secretly allied himself with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.
units.literal: Late in Zhonghe, because Li Keyong of Taiyuan's military power was then flourishing, he secretly formed a pact with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.

units.zh: 克用怒，加兵討之。
units.en: Keyong was furious and sent additional troops to punish him.
units.literal: Keyong was enraged and added troops to campaign against him.

units.zh: 赫連鐸據雲中，屢引匡威與河東爭雲、代，並兵積年。
units.en: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into conflict with Hedong over Yunzhou and Daizhou; their armies fought for years.
units.literal: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into contest with Hedong over Yun and Dai; their armies clashed for years.

units.zh: 可舉慮其窺伺山東，終為己患，遂遣使構雲中赫連鐸乘其背，則與鎮州合謀舉兵，兼言易、定是燕、趙之餘，雲得其地則正其疆理而分之。
units.en: Keju feared that Keyong would turn his ambitions toward the eastern provinces and become a lasting threat. He sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to attack Keyong from the rear, then conspired with the forces of Zhenzhou to raise troops. He argued that Yizhou and Dingzhou were the last holdings of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yunzhong gained those lands their boundaries could be redrawn and the territory divided.
units.literal: Keju feared that Keyong would watch for an opening in the Shandong region and in the end become a threat to him; he therefore sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to strike from the rear, then conspired with Zhenzhou to raise troops, also saying that Yi and Ding were the remnant territories of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yun gained those lands their boundaries could be rectified and divided.

units.zh: 景福初，鎮州王鎔誘河東將李存孝。
units.en: Early in the Jingfu era Wang Rong of Zhenzhou won over the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jingfu reign, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou enticed the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.

units.zh: 二年春，河東復出師井陘，再乞師，匡威來援。
units.en: In the spring of the second year Hedong again marched through Jingxing Pass. Wang Rong again appealed for help, and Kuangwei came to his aid.
units.literal: In spring of the second year Hedong again marched out through Jingxing; Rong again begged for troops, and Kuangwei came to his aid.

units.zh: 曾祖秀，祖珍，父讓，皆爲本州軍校。
units.en: His great-grandfather Xiu, grandfather Zhen, and father Rang had all been army officers in the prefecture.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Xiu, grandfather Zhen, and father Rang had all been army officers of the prefecture.

units.zh: 有次將劉仁恭者，多權數；
units.en: Among the deputy generals was Liu Rengong, a man of many stratagems.
units.literal: Among the deputy generals was one Liu Rengong, full of stratagems.

units.zh: 攻之彌月不下，乃穴地道以入。
units.en: After a month of siege the city still held, so they dug a tunnel to enter it.
units.literal: They besieged it for a full month without taking it, then dug a tunnel to enter.

units.zh: 時可舉遣將李全忠攻易州。
units.en: Keju then sent the general Li Quanzhong to attack Yizhou.
units.literal: At that time Keju sent the general Li Quanzhong to attack Yizhou.

units.zh: 大學士王鐸深知之，鐸罷相失職，樞亦久之不調。
units.en: Grand Academician Wang Duo thought highly of him; when Duo lost his chancellorship and his position, Shu also went long without reassignment.
units.literal: Grand Academician Wang Duo thought highly of him; when Duo lost his chancellorship and his position, Shu also went long without reassignment.

units.zh: 中和初，王鐸復見用，以舊恩徙為鄭滑掌書記、檢校司封郎中，賜金紫，入朝歷兵、吏二員外郎。
units.en: At the beginning of Zhonghe, Wang Duo was again employed; out of old kindness Shu was transferred to chief secretary of Zheng-Hua and acting director of the Department of Feudal Ranks, granted gold seal and purple robe; entering court he served successively as vice director in the ministries of War and Personnel.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe, Wang Duo was again employed; out of old kindness Shu was transferred to chief secretary of Zheng-Hua and acting Director of the Department of Feudal Ranks, granted gold seal and purple robe; entering court he served successively as vice director in the Ministries of War and Personnel.

units.zh: 朝廷時遣河中帥李執方、滄州帥劉約各遣使勸令歸闕，別俟朝旨。
units.en: The court had Li Zhifang of Hezhong and Liu Yue of Cangzhou each send envoys urging him to come to court and await further imperial orders.
units.literal: The court at the time had the commanders of Hezhong, Li Zhifang, and Cangzhou, Liu Yue, each send envoys urging him to return to court and await separate court orders.

units.zh: 曾祖孝物，祖俊，並本州軍校。
units.en: His great-grandfather Xiaowu and his grandfather Jun had both been army officers in their home prefecture.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Xiaowu and grandfather Jun were both army officers of the prefecture.

units.zh: 何進滔，靈武人也。
units.en: He Jintao came from Lingwu.
units.literal: He Jintao was a native of Lingwu.

units.zh: 父默，夏州衙前兵馬使，檢校太子賓客，試太常卿。
units.en: His father Mo had served as horse-and-foot commissioner before the Xiazhou yamen, with the ranks of Acting Crown Prince's Guest and Acting Minister of Ceremonies.
units.literal: His father Mo was Cavalry and Infantry Commissioner before the Xiazhou yamen, Acting Crown Prince's Guest, and Acting Taichang Qing.

units.zh: 憲誠心不自安，乃遣子孝章入覲，又飛章願以所管奉命。
units.en: Uneasy in his own mind, Xiancheng sent his son Xiaozhang to court and dispatched urgent memorials offering to place his command under the throne's orders.
units.literal: Xiancheng felt ill at ease in his heart; he then sent his son Xiaozhang to court for audience, and also sent urgent memorials offering to place his jurisdiction under court command.

units.zh: 憲誠子 孝章孝章，幼聰悟好學。
units.en: Xiancheng's son Xiaozhang was clever from childhood and devoted to study.
units.literal: Xiancheng's son Xiaozhang — from youth he was clever and fond of learning.

units.zh: 孝章倡言願效文職，醞奇之，令攝府參軍。
units.en: Xiaozhang spoke up saying he wished to serve in the civil branch; Yun was impressed and appointed him acting headquarters adjutant.
units.literal: Xiaozhang openly declared that he wished to serve in a civil post; Yun was struck by this and had him act as staff adjutant of the headquarters.

units.zh: 及憲誠領節鉞，改士曹參軍、兼監察御史，賜緋。
units.en: When Xiancheng took the command baton, Xiaozhang was made Staff Officer of the Personnel Section and concurrent Investigating Censor, with scarlet robes bestowed on him.
